articles.title: Caregiver creep: how helping elderly relatives can snowball into a full-time job
articles.summary: Assisting an ageing loved one can start with small tasks but may lead to full-time caregiving that requires more support. Helping an ageing parent or loved one often begins with easy-to-field requests: Pick up a prescription. Drive them to a doctor’s appointment. Grab groceries.
body: However, light tasks – just “helping out” here and there – may eventually snowball into the avalanche of full-time caregiving, a phenomenon becoming known as “caregiver creep”. Like “ caregiver burnout ”, it’s not a formal term, but there is growing awareness about this slow build among healthcare providers and experts.

A 2025 research report from the AARP and the National Alliance for Caregiving found that 63 million Americans act as caregivers; one in every four adults is a caregiver and the majority (94%) are caring for an adult. As the population ages – the oldest baby boomers will turn 80 this year – the need for care will increase.

The US Bureau of Labor Statistics reports the majority (59%) of those providing this unpaid care are women. Many gen X and millennial women are feeling the sandwich-generation squeeze of caring for parents and children on top of their careers.

Recognizing when responsibilities increase, how to identify when support needs to level up, and where to find resources both for the person receiving care and the caregiver can help manage caregiver creep.

articles.title: A job that changed me: Being a theatre usher cracked open my heart to beauty
articles.summary: The performances often gave me goose bumps, but I also got to observe the highs and lows of audience behaviour. I was 24, had just moved into a share house I couldn’t afford, and my job as a nanny was proving less than ideal.
body: A friend had told me to apply to become a front-of-house staff member at Australia’s busiest performing arts centre, Arts Centre Melbourne. It was a rare opportunity, as people rarely quit. To be surrounded by art again sounded like a dream.

I progressed to the final interview round. Anxious about nailing it and unable to study for it – for some unknown reason, a maths quiz was involved – I focused purely on appearance. I blew my budget on a blow wave, planning to charm the interviewers with my perfect hair and Target office-casual best.
Whether it was my hair or the secret texts to my friend asking for help answering the maths quiz, I got the job.

articles.title: Met Gala exhibition honoring John Galliano is cancelled after backlash
articles.summary: Fashion designer was convicted of hate crime by French court in 2011 after series of racist and antisemitic remarks. The controversial fashion designer John Galliano announced on Monday that an exhibition honoring his work that New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art had scheduled to open for the…
body: The museum’s decision to honor Galliano, who was convicted of a hate crime by a French court in 2011 after a series of racist and antisemitic remarks, had drawn controversy and backlash.

“After much reflection and discussion with all those involved, I have decided, with great sadness, that it is best for the exhibition not to take place at this time,” Galliano wrote in a statement posted on Instagram on Monday morning.
The exhibition, titled John Galliano: Horizons, was announced in early August and was set to have been kicked off by the annual Met Gala.

In his statement on Monday saying that the exhibition was off, Galliano wrote: “I remain fully accountable for the pain caused by my words in the past, particularly the hurt I caused to the Jewish and Asian communities, and I remain deeply sorry.

articles.title: How to Style the Ballet Heel Like an It Girl
articles.summary: The ballet heel has amassed a loyal following in Kaia Gerber, Zoë Kravitz, and Apple Martin. Here’s how to style the beloved French girl shoe for fall.
body: Are ballet pumps the ultimate It girl shoe? It certainly seems like it. Lately, they’ve been spotted on all of our favorite celebs-about-town. Think Kaia Gerber, Lily-Rose Depp, Hailey Bieber, and Zoë Kravitz, for whom the style has become something of a signature.

Of course, we understand the appeal. Part ballerina, part pump, the style combines the gamine energy of your favorite flats with the limb-elongating power of a classic heel. They look great with everything from mini dresses and skirts to off-duty denim and even more artful ensembles. And they’re practical, too: the low, block-style heel is comfortable enough for running errands and hitting the town.
Championed by the likes of Repetto, Maryam Nassir Zadeh, and Maison Margiela, the ballet heel has become a style staple of the downtown set. Shop our favorites, and see how we’d style them, here.
The ultimate cool girl shoe meets the ultimate cool girl combo: jeans and a tee. Just add an It bag and timeless accessories.

articles.title: In Guadalajara, Chasing Art, Fantastic Food, and the Love of a Good Time
articles.summary: Mexico's second city is the birthplace of many of its cultural cornerstones, from mariachi to tequila. Longtime visitor Michael Snyder returns to dive deep into its world-class culinary and craft scenes.
body: The second day of my first trip to Guadalajara, a decade ago, began, like so many mornings in Mexico's second city do: with blazing sunshine and a blazing hangover. I'd spent the previous evening sipping agave distillates at Mezonte, a miniature plywood-clad tasting room that pours some of Mexico's most exciting spirits, and dancing clumsily at what may be the world's most perfectly named bar: Pare de Sufrir, or Stop Suffering. My inevitable headache required an antidote. And so, in the fine expiatory fashion of this famously Catholic, famously hedonistic metropolis of nearly six million, I chose sublimity.
The ornate Guadalajara Cathedral mixes neo-Gothic, Baroque, and Spanish Renaissance architectural styles.
Murals by José Clemente Orozco adorn the central dome of the Hospicio Cabañas.

body: That variety is precisely why I set out to find the best protein bars for every type of protein bar eater. I polled fellow staffers, scoured local grocery stores, and tasted my way through bars of all kinds, and in so doing found over a dozen I can vouch for. The category has come a long way from the PowerBar of the ’90s, and the taste profiles of protein bars in 2026 are so varied that even the most epicurean among us can find an option we like. Whether you’re into bars that taste practically homemade, or you’d rather your protein bar look and taste as much like a candy bar as possible, I’ve got you covered.

The 16 bars I recommend include a variety of protein sources that will keep you full. articles.title: First, End Your Marriage. Then, Cook Rice.
articles.summary: “The first night I spent in the sublet apartment, separate from my children, separated from my husband and home of 24 years, I cooked and my sister came over.”
body: My sister, Nina, had to wear me down to have her over, so reluctant was I to be the reason she had to leave her small children and drag ass to this stranger’s apartment. I’m fine, I’ll be fine, I like being alone, you don’t have to come. Nina persisted. Finally, I admitted, Yes, I would like you to be here and, no, I don’t think I should be by myself.

I met my husband when I was 23, got married when I was 26, and was happy in my marriage for more years than I was not. But our average had plummeted: too many lows in a row. For several years, I had made a lot of pragmatic choices I hoped would make our relationship better: If I was unhappy, I should work on that. I found the right therapist and showed up every week. I accepted my brain’s delightful chemical mix of depression and anxiety and got treatment for both. I stopped smoking weed. I tried to be a better parent. I started lifting heavy weights and the back pain I’d carried around for almost two decades went away. I wrote two cookbooks that did very well, and I became a video host.
